summary: Conotoxin-derived cosmetic active developed into clinically tested skin-care products.
editor_note: Instead of relying only on cosmetic positioning, the company centers its products on a defined conotoxin-derived peptide and publishes a 60-person, six-month randomized double-blind placebo-controlled study. That is useful evidence of craft, but the study appears on a company surface rather than an independent journal, so efficacy and generalizability should remain qualified.
why_featured: A defined peptide behind the products

sources.label: Science4Beauty official shop and product site

product_evidence.claim: The company science page identifies a conotoxin-derived active and reports a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled six-month study with 60 volunteers.
The public shop and development project connect the active to sold skin-care products and a funded commercialization program.
The investor announcement identifies 4growth VC as lead and Hard2beat as a participant in a PLN 7 million investment round.

market_context.primary_user: Consumers buying evidence-led anti-aging skin-care products and beauty brands evaluating peptide actives.
market_context.differentiation: A defined conotoxin-derived peptide platform linked to finished products and a disclosed controlled study.
market_context.why_now: The investment funds international commercialization and continued development of the active platform.

risks.claim: The controlled study is described by the company rather than an independent publication, and 60 participants limit generalizability.
risks.basis: VentureDex assessment based on the company science page and investor announcement.

unnamed_round_assessment.reason: The investor announcement verifies a PLN 7 million investment led by 4growth VC with Hard2beat participating, but it does not state a canonical round name. VentureDex records Unspecified rather than inferring Seed while retaining product, study and commercialization evidence.
